brief.title: Business card: Maya Okafor, Product Designer
brief.brief:
Design a two-sided US business card (3.5 x 2 in) for Maya Okafor, Product Designer. Front: her name and title. Back: her contact details, email maya@example.com and website example.com/maya. Those are the only facts: do not add a phone number, address, company, social handles or anything else.

Deliver both sides as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the front and the back as cards that scale fluidly to fit a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling; you may add a short screen-only note beside the cards (not on them) stating the trim size and how to print. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: 3.5in 2in; margin: 0 } so it prints as exactly two pages, page 1 the front and page 2 the back, each filling its page, with any screen-only notes hidden.

requirements.description: The front of the card shows the name "Maya Okafor" and the title "Product Designer".
The back of the card shows the email maya@example.com and the website example.com/maya.
Presents the card as two distinct sides, a front and a back.
Contains no invented contact details or facts: no phone number, address, company or social handles.

artifacts.title: Business Card: Maya Okafor, Product Designer

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: correct name, title, email and website, two distinct sides, and no invented details.

checks.reason: The front section shows the h1 'Maya Okafor' and the title 'Product Designer' (rendered uppercase via CSS, text is present in the markup and visible in both screenshots).
The back section contains a mailto link reading 'maya@example.com' and a link reading 'example.com/maya', both visible in the desktop and phone screenshots.
Two distinct section elements, labelled Front of card and Back of card, with separate print rules placing the front and back on separate pages.

No phone number, address, company or social handles appear; the only contact details are the supplied email and website. The eyebrow 'Product Design' is a label restating the title rather than an invented fact.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, restrained card with the supplied facts only: the name and title on a cream front, the email and website on a darker tinted back. It reads clearly on both desktop and phone with no horizontal overflow.
strengths: Front uses a large serif name with a small uppercase title and accent rule, giving a clear hierarchy.
Back shows labelled Email and Website entries with underlined links, easy to scan.
Phone layout at 390px fits without sideways scrolling and keeps both cards at the 3.5:2 ratio.
weaknesses: The eyebrow 'Product Design' on the front repeats the title and adds a line the brief did not ask for.
The back's accent rule sits at the top, leaving the lower half of the card empty on the front and back alike.
Print styles are defined but the print result was not checked, so the two-page output is unverified.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a minimal, print-ready card with only the supplied contact details and a warm, paper-like palette.

artifacts.title: Business Card: Maya Okafor, Product Designer

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: both sides show the supplied details, and nothing is invented.

checks.reason: The front article contains the h2 'Maya Okafor' and the paragraph 'Product Designer', both visible in the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back card shows 'maya@example.com' and 'example.com/maya' under the Contact label, visible in both screenshots.
Two separate article elements (.front and .back) are rendered as distinct cards, with print rules forcing a page break after the front so each side prints on its own page.
The card text contains only the supplied name, title, email and website. The intro and note add no phone, address, company or social handles.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, faithful two-sided card that uses only the supplied details and lays out without sideways scrolling on a 390px phone. The pastel gradients and decorative circles give it a soft, friendly look.
strengths: Front shows the name and title in clear bold hierarchy on a mint-to-lavender gradient.
Back uses only the supplied email and website, with a small Contact label and a footer line.
Print CSS sets a 3.5in x 2in page size, forces a page break between sides, and hides the screen notes.
weaknesses: The decorative circles are placed on the card edges and slightly overlap the back's contact label area, which may look cluttered when…
The back's footer repeats the name and title, so the back carries little beyond the supplied contact details.
Print sizing uses fixed pt values that were not verified on a physical printer.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a soft, pastel, minimal card that sticks strictly to the supplied details.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements: front and back contents are correct, the two sides are distinct, and no invented details appear.

checks.reason: The front card shows the h1 'Maya Okafor' and the title 'Product Designer' (rendered uppercase via CSS, text in the source is 'Product Designer'), visible in the desktop and phone screenshots.
The back card shows 'maya@example.com' as a mailto link and 'example.com/maya' as a website link, both visible in both screenshots.
Front and back are presented as two separate section cards with labels FRONT and BACK, and print CSS sets page-break-after so they print as two pages.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, faithful two-sided card that shows only the supplied details, with a bold orange front and a black back that stays legible at 390px with no sideways overflow.

Back shows email and website with small orange labels, giving a clear hierarchy in the phone and desktop screenshots.

weaknesses: The back is fairly plain: a small orange rule and two lines of text, with a lot of empty black space.
The front title sits small in the bottom-left corner, so it reads much weaker than the name.
The on-screen note is long and repeats the print instructions at the top of the page.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a bold, minimal card with only the essential contact details and no extra graphics.
